messages:
maria.k: Heads-up — spotted a batch issue: about ~18 invoices from the 2026-03-23 billing run are missing compute/GPU line items (reserved and on-demand). example: inv_00492a (acme-corp). :eyes:
ajay.s: Ugh. Is this the new batch runner or the post-process that materializes lineitems? Which job id did it use?
maria.k: Batch job id `batch-2026-03-23-09z` (see logs). Quick CSV snippet from S3 (headers trimmed):
```
invoice_id,customer,product,amount
inv_00492a,acme-corp,storage,1200
inv_00492a,acme-corp,tax,96
```
(notice: compute rows missing where we usually have `compute.gpu` lines)
claire.f: We also got reports of duplicate PDFs for 3 accounts — same invoice number but two PDF attachments sent. Customers: fluxcorp, bluefjord, velox. Reputational risk. :warning:
billing-bot: Automated check: batch-2026-03-23-09z processed. 18 invoices flagged: missing_expected_product_rows, 3 invoices flagged: duplicate_pdf_generated. IDs: inv_00492a, inv_00495b, inv_00499c, ... (full list in /billing/alerts/1769534321).
oliver: I saw a retry path that runs an asynchronous reconciliation for lineitems. Possible race where the `usage-aggregation` job finished after invoice emission and the post-emit reconciliation failed to attach rows. Pinging billing-service deploys: last rollout `main@b5d9c3` at 1769531200.
ajay.s: Can we check the `emitInvoice` call traces? If the aggregator wasn't ready, we should detect and enqueue for re-emit rather than emit empty. Can someone grab the logs: `grep "emitInvoice" /var/logs/billing/batch-2026-03-23.log | tail -n 200`
maria.k: Paste of a failing trace (sanitized):
```
[09:12:02] emitInvoice(inv_00492a) status=EMITTED total=1296 line_items=2
[09:12:03] reconcileUsage(inv_00492a) status=FAILED reason=AggregateNotReady
```
This shows emission happened before reconcile.
claire.f: For the duplicate PDFs — looks like the `pdf-service` got a retry signal and re-sent. Not sure why invoice status didn't flip to DRAFT before re-emit.
emma: Ok — we need remediation plan and approvals for any re-issuance. High level: 1) Stop auto-send for batch-2026-03-23; 2) Identify affected invoices and mark as DRAFT; 3) Run reconcile then re-emit & send. Approve manual reissue for customers > $5k? :+1:
ajay.s: Agree. I'll take point on a dry-run reconcile first to ensure no double-bill. Proposed steps:
- run `billing:reconcile --batch batch-2026-03-23-09z --dry-run --output /tmp/recon-1769534321.json`
- review diffs for top 50 invoices
- if green, mark DRAFT and re-emit via `billing:emit --batch ... --force` with `--no-email` for a first pass, then send PDFs after manual QA.
maria.k: I started the dry-run (triggered at 1769534800). Output path: s3://billing/recons/dry-recon-1769534321.json. Preliminary: 18 invoices would gain 1-6 line items and total increases vary (one spike +$18k).
claire.f: For customers already emailed: recommended customer support outreach before re-send. I'll draft templates. Also need accounting sign-off on changes >$10k.
oliver: Engineering note: we'll add a guard to delay emission until `usage-aggregation` promises completion or returns explicit `no-more-rows`. I'll open a PR to gate `emitInvoice`. Won't ship hotfix the same day, but can patch the batch runner to hold for 2m.
emma: Approve reissue for affected customers with net change <= $10k automatically. For > $10k, hold and route to finance approvals queue. Claire, cc finance-approvals. Maria/Ajay, proceed with dry-run QA and report back.
claire.f: Got it. I'll queue support messages and prepare refund/credit workflows in case net is negative.
maria.k: Will post final dry-run summary in this thread (uploading the recon JSON now). Thanks all, triage in progress. :shipit:
